_note: Hand-authored analyst assumptions (ESTIMATES, not data). Edited by hand; NOT overwritten by the fetch scripts. Growth/margins are fractions. 'yr1/yr2 growth' default to Yahoo consensus revenue estimates unless overridden.
erpSource: Equity risk premium ~4.5%: close to Damodaran's implied ERP for the S&P 500 (2025-26 range ~4.3-4.6%).
crpNote: Argentina country-risk premium = full J.P. Morgan EMBI spread for Argentina, 648 bp at the close of 2026-10-16 (Rava / argentinadatos), added to the cost of equity of YPF and GGAL (lambda = 1).
probDefault: Scenario probabilities are subjective analyst judgments informed by the catalysts listed; they sum to 100%.

META.precedentNote: Mega-cap internet control deals are rare (antitrust); range anchored on large strategic tech deals such as Microsoft-LinkedIn (2016, ~$26B) and Microsoft-Activision Blizzard (2023, ~$69B). A takeover of META is not realistic; the M&A view is a theoretical 'private-market value' cross-check.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: AI capex ($130-145B guided for 2026) does not earn its cost of capital; ad growth slows to mid-single digits and D&A from the data-center build compresses margins.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus revenue for 2026-27, then low-double-digit growth; AI improves ad ranking and pricing, while capex intensity normalizes from ~54% of revenue to ~20% by year 6.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Meta AI and business agents monetize (click-to-message, WhatsApp), plus a compute-for-hire business; operating leverage returns.

scenarios.name: Tail: AI super-cycle
scenarios.desc: Personal-agent platform becomes a new revenue pillar (subscriptions + enterprise compute), and revenue compounds near 20%.

scenarios.name: Tail: Regulatory shock
scenarios.desc: EU DMA 'pay-or-consent' limits plus US youth-safety/privacy litigation and FTC remedies curb ad targeting; ~$25B in fines/settlements (2026 Q2 already booked $2.4B of legal charges).

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings (guide $61-64B revenue) and 2027 capex outlook
FY2026 results; first 2027 expense/capex guide
EU DMA compliance decisions / US FTC and state AG youth-safety cases
Meta AI / business-agent monetization disclosure (ARPU uplift)

score.rationale: Quality: best-in-class ad platform with ~41% operating margin (FY2025) and >3B daily users; a net-cash-light balance sheet after the AI build-out is still investment-grade. Growth: consensus has revenue +26% in 2026 and +21% in 2027, exceptional for a $1.9T company. Risk: the main risk is capital intensity (2026 capex is ~55% of revenue, which drove Q2 FCF down to $0.8B) and regulation (EU DMA, youth-safety suits). Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside.

UNH.precedentNote: Managed-care precedents: CVS-Aetna (2018, ~$69B), Cigna-Express Scripts (2018, ~$67B), UnitedHealth-Change Healthcare (2022, ~$13B). Sector control deals have typically cleared around 10-14x EBITDA (estimate). UNH's own takeover is implausible because of its size; this is a private-market cross-check.
UNH.betaNote: The 5Y beta (0.62) understates the risk now that the business is impaired; an assumed 0.85 is used (editable).

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: Medical cost trend stays ~8-10%; 2028 Medicare Advantage rates disappoint and Optum Health value-based care stays loss-making. Margins stuck near 4-5%.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Repricing plus a final 2027 MA rate of +2.48% (~5% effective incl. risk-score trend), and benefit cuts and exits restore margins to ~6.5% by year 5, still below the 8%+ of 2022-23.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Cost trend normalizes, MA rate tailwinds continue and Optum recovers. Margins return toward the historical ~8%.

scenarios.name: Tail: DOJ / False Claims outcome
scenarios.desc: The criminal and civil DOJ probes into MA billing and risk-adjustment coding (see the Senate Grassley report, Jan 2026) end in a large settlement (~$30B assumed) and coding restrictions.

scenarios.name: Tail: MA risk-adjustment overhaul
scenarios.desc: CMS extends the exclusion of chart-review and in-home HRA diagnoses (already partly applied in 2027 rates), structurally lowering MA revenue per member.

catalysts.event: FY2026 results and 2027 EPS guidance
CMS CY2028 Medicare Advantage Advance Notice
CMS CY2028 final Rate Announcement
DOJ criminal and civil probes into MA billing
Medical care ratio (MCR) vs. guidance: utilization and cost trend

score.rationale: Quality: unmatched scale (FY2025 revenue $448B) and the Optum vertical integration; however, operating margin fell from 8.7% (2023) to 4.2% (2025). Growth: consensus has 2026 revenue roughly flat and 2027 at +3%, the weakest growth in decades. Risk: elevated, with DOJ criminal and civil probes, political scrutiny of MA coding, and a cost trend running above rate increases. Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside.

DIS.precedentNote: Media precedents: Disney-21st Century Fox (2019, ~$71B), Discovery-WarnerMedia (2022, ~$43B), Amazon-MGM (2022, ~$8.5B), Skydance-Paramount (2025, ~$8B). Content and IP-rich assets have typically traded around 10-14x EBITDA in control deals (estimate).

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: Linear TV declines faster, ESPN DTC cannibalizes affiliate fees, the parks cycle softens and the $60B Experiences capex plan earns lower returns.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus FY26-27 (+7.5% / +4.5%); streaming margins expand toward double digits; Experiences grows mid-single digits.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Streaming reaches ~15% margins and the franchise slate (Marvel, Star Wars, Pixar) lifts Studio and Consumer Products; new cruise ships and park expansions ramp.

scenarios.name: Tail: Avengers: Doomsday mega-hit
scenarios.desc: Avengers: Doomsday (wide release Dec 18, 2026; global presales >$100M) grosses ~$2.8B worldwide vs ~$1.6B assumed in the base case. Spider-Man: Brand New Day (Sony-distributed, Jul 31, 2026) already lifted Marvel merchandise and Disney+ hours. Incremental income flows through FY2027 quarters (see the timing chart) and adds a franchise halo.

scenarios.name: Tail: Linear collapse + consumer recession
scenarios.desc: Cord-cutting accelerates sharply and park attendance falls in a US recession.

score.rationale: Quality: unrivaled IP library plus a parks moat; operating margin improved from 8% (FY22) to 15% (FY25) as streaming turned profitable. Growth: consensus has mid-single-digit growth (FY26 +7.5%, FY27 +4.5%). Risk: moderate, with ~$41B of net debt, structural linear-TV decline and a heavy Experiences capex cycle (~8.5% of revenue). Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside. A single blockbuster is worth well under $1/share as a one-off (see the timing chart); sustained franchise strength matters far more than one release.

NIO.precedentNote: Auto and EV precedents are sales-based, because many targets are loss-making: Geely-Volvo Cars (2010, $1.8B), Stellantis-Leapmotor 21% stake (2023, ~€1.5B), VW-XPeng ~5% stake (2023, ~$0.7B). scenarios.name: Base

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Three brands scale and battery swap (>3,000 stations, plus 1,000 more in 2026) becomes a moat and a partner network; exports to Europe and the Middle East grow.

score.rationale: Quality: still loss-making at the operating level (FY2025 EBIT margin −16%), though the Q2 2026 gross margin reached 18.4% with four straight quarters of positive operating cash flow. Growth: very high, with consensus revenue +47% in 2026 and +19% in 2027. Risk: very high, given a brutal China price war, repeated dilution, policy dependence and geopolitical/ADR risk. Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside, with very wide dispersion.

YPF.sector: Argentine integrated oil & gas (Vaca Muerta shale)
YPF.betaNote: Yahoo's 5Y beta (-0.11) is meaningless for a state-controlled ADR; an assumed 1.1 (integrated oil, moderately levered) is used, plus the 6.48% Argentina EMBI as country risk.
YPF.growthNote: Year 1 (FY2026) = H1 2026 reported revenue $11.52B + ~$11.5B H2 at the guided ~$75 Brent ≈ $23B (+26% in USD). Year 2 assumes Brent normalizing toward ~$70 offsets shale volume growth (≈ -2%). Yahoo consensus for YPF is in ARS and is not used for USD growth.
YPF.precedentNote: Argentine upstream deals have priced at roughly 3.5-6x EV/EBITDA (estimate): Pluspetrol's purchase of ExxonMobil's Vaca Muerta assets (2024, ~$1B), Vista's acquisition of Petronas' 50% of La Amarga Chica (2025, ~$1.2B incl. shares) and YPF's farm-outs. A takeover of YPF is not realistic (51% held by the State under the 2012 expropriation law); the M&A view is a theoretical private-market cross-check.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: Brent falls to ~$60, the shale ramp slips (pipeline/rig constraints) and domestic fuel prices lag import parity again; EBIT margin ~13%.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: 2026 at the ~$8B EBITDA guide (Brent ~$82), then Brent ~$70; shale oil from 215 kbbl/d (2026 avg, 250 exit) toward the LLL Oil plateau (~240 kbbl/d for that project alone by 2032) via the VMOS export pipeline; mature-field exits keep lifting costs ~$8/boe.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Vaca Muerta becomes an export platform: VMOS on time, LLL Oil approved under RIGI, Argentina LNG reaches FID, and fuel pricing stays at import parity.

scenarios.name: Tail: Macro crisis / devaluation
scenarios.desc: A disorderly devaluation and the return of export duties, fuel-price freezes and FX controls (2019-style); country risk widens by ~400 bp and margins compress for years.

scenarios.name: Tail: Petersen/Burford case revived
scenarios.desc: The US Supreme Court takes Petersen/Eton Park's October 2026 petition and reinstates the $16.1B judgment against the Republic (the Second Circuit voided it on 2026-03-27 and confirmed YPF itself is not liable). Turnover of the State's 51% stake would hit governance and sovereign risk; ~$1.5B of assumed legal/financing costs plus a wider country-risk premium.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results: shale ramp vs 250 kbbl/d exit target, FCF vs ~$2B guide
US Supreme Court cert decision on the Petersen/Eton Park petition ($16.1B judgment vs Argentina)
VMOS export pipeline start-up; RIGI approval of the LLL Oil project (~$25B capex over 15 years)
Argentine presidential election (fuel-pricing and export-duty regime)
Brent price (2026 guide assumes ~$82 average, $75 for H2)

score.rationale: Quality: Argentina's largest integrated producer; record Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $2.8B (43% margin), lifting cost down to ~$8/boe and net leverage of 1.1x. Growth: high, from Vaca Muerta shale (+47% y/y in Q2 2026) and export projects. Risk: high, given Argentine macro and policy risk, State control (51%), Brent exposure and the long tail of the expropriation litigation. Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside.

GGAL.sector: Argentine financial group (bank, cards, insurance, asset management)
GGAL.betaNote: Yahoo's 5Y beta (0.29) reflects local trading frictions; an assumed 1.15 (EM bank) is used, plus the 6.48% Argentina EMBI as country risk.
GGAL.precedentNote: Argentine bank control deals have priced well below LatAm norms (estimates): Grupo Galicia's purchase of HSBC Argentina (2024, ~$550M, below book), Banco Macro's purchase of Itaú Argentina (2023, ~$50M) and BBVA/others' minority deals; LatAm control deals in normal times ~1.0-1.5x book. Range used: 0.5-1.3x P/BV.
GGAL.compsNote: P/BV is the primary bank multiple. Peer P/E is TTM while GGAL's TTM earnings are depressed (ROE ~2% after the 2025 disinflation and credit-loss cycle), so P/E is applied to the FY2026e consensus EPS and shown for reference only; the triangulated fair value uses P/BV comps.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: Non-performing loans stay ~10% (Q2 2026: 10.6%), loan growth stalls and margins compress as rates fall; sustainable ROE ~12%, below the cost of equity.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus EPS for 2026-27, credit quality normalizes, the HSBC (Galicia Más) integration savings stick; ROE converges to ~18% in USD terms and book value grows ~10%/yr.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Financial deepening: private credit/GDP rises from ~10% toward LatAm levels (~30-40%), with lower funding costs and fee growth (Naranja X); ROE ~22%.

scenarios.name: Tail: Macro crisis / devaluation
scenarios.desc: Disorderly devaluation: inflation re-accelerates (IAS 29 monetary losses), NPLs spike and USD book value shrinks; country risk widens by ~400 bp.

scenarios.name: Tail: Regulatory shock
scenarios.desc: Return of interest-rate caps, higher reserve requirements or forced Treasury financing, or a windfall/bank tax; ~$0.4B one-off hit to equity.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results: NPL trend (10.6% in Q2), ROE vs 11.3% in Q2
INDEC CPI and BCRA rate decisions (funding cost, monetary-position loss)
Argentina EMBI spread (648 bp on 2026-10-16) and the official FX band
Argentine presidential election

score.rationale: Quality: Argentina's largest private financial group (~16% share of private loans and deposits), capital ratio 23.7% and efficiency 35% in Q2 2026. Growth: credit penetration is among the lowest in LatAm, so loan growth can be strong if disinflation holds. Risk: high, given NPLs at 10.6%, IAS 29 inflation accounting, FX and sovereign exposure, and regulatory history. Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside.

MU.betaNote: Yahoo's 5Y beta (2.23) is inflated by the 2026 memory squeeze; an assumed 1.6 (cyclical semiconductor) is used.
MU.growthNote: Fiscal years end on the Thursday closest to 31 August (FY2026 = 53 weeks ended 2026-09-03). FY2026 is taken from the 10-K via SEC XBRL because Yahoo's annual statements stop at FY2025. Year 1 / year 2 = consensus FY2027 / FY2028 revenue ($275.5B / $318.9B). Memory is highly cyclical, so years 3-5 assume DRAM/NAND pricing normalizes (Base −12%/yr) and the steady-state EBIT margin is a mid-cycle 38%, versus 74.6% in FY2026 and roughly 25% on average over FY2016-25 (HBM mix and long-term supply agreements justify a higher mid-cycle than history).
MU.precedentNote: Memory control deals have cleared around 5-8x mid-cycle EBITDA (estimates): Western Digital-SanDisk (2016, ~$19B), the Bain-led Toshiba Memory (Kioxia) buyout (2018, ~$18B), SK Hynix-Intel NAND/Solidigm (2020-21, $9B). Because TTM EBITDA is at a cyclical peak, a lower 4-7x is applied. A takeover of MU is not realistic (size, CFIUS, China SAMR); this is a private-market cross-check.
MU.compsNote: Comps statistics use SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics (a conglomerate: memory, foundry, phones), WDC and SNDK. NVDA and AMD are shown for reference only (AI compute customers, not memory peers) and excluded from the medians. All multiples are on TTM figures at a memory-cycle peak, so they overstate mid-cycle value.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: Industry capacity additions (Samsung, SK Hynix, CXMT) and HBM qualification wins by rivals turn DRAM into oversupply from 2028; prices fall sharply and margins return to the historical ~25% average.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus FY2027-28 (+107% / +16%) as AI servers absorb HBM and high-capacity DRAM; then pricing normalizes over FY2029-31 and the margin settles at a mid-cycle 38%, above history thanks to HBM mix and long-term agreements.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: HBM4/HBM4E share above 25%, multi-year take-or-pay contracts with hyperscalers and disciplined industry capex keep the downturn shallow.

scenarios.name: Tail: AI capex bust / memory crash
scenarios.desc: Hyperscaler AI capex is cut in 2027 (ROI disappointment), inventory piled up at customers is dumped and contract prices halve; a 2023-style downturn on a much larger revenue base.

scenarios.name: Tail: Memory-bound AI super-cycle
scenarios.desc: Memory bandwidth becomes the binding constraint of AI compute (agentic inference, long context); demand outruns supply for years and the cycle flattens into a growth market.

scenarios.name: Tail: Taiwan / East Asia geopolitical shock
scenarios.desc: A blockade or conflict around Taiwan, where Micron makes most of its DRAM and HBM (Taichung, Taoyuan); ~$40B of assumed asset losses and rebuild costs, supply chaos and a higher risk premium.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler (MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN) Q3 results and 2027 capex guides
FQ1 FY2027 results and FQ2 guide (consensus revenue ~$61.7B)
DRAM/NAND contract prices (TrendForce) and HBM4 qualification news
US/China export controls (China banned Micron in CII in 2023), CHIPS Act milestones (Idaho, New York fabs)

score.rationale: Quality: one of three DRAM/HBM makers, net cash, FY2026 operating margin 74.6% at the top of the cycle. Growth: consensus doubles revenue in FY2027 on HBM and AI server demand. Risk: memory is the most cyclical part of semis (FY2023 operating loss of $5.4B), and Taiwan concentration plus China export policy add tail risk. Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside on mid-cycle margins.

ASML.growthNote: ASML reports in EUR (US GAAP 20-F). The model is computed in EUR and converted to USD per ADR (1 ADR = 1 ordinary share) at the ECB euro reference rate stored in valuation.json. Year 1 / year 2 = consensus FY2026 / FY2027 net sales (€44.5B / €57.2B, +36% / +29%).
ASML.precedentNote: Semiconductor-equipment control deals (estimates): ASML-Cymer (2013, ~$3.7B), KLA-Orbotech (2019, ~$3.4B), and the abandoned AMAT-Tokyo Electron (2015) and Lam-KLA (2016) mergers, around 15-25x EBITDA. A takeover of ASML is not realistic (monopoly in EUV, Dutch/EU strategic asset); this is a private-market cross-check.
ASML.compsNote: Comps statistics use AMAT, LRCX and KLAC. Tokyo Electron (8035.T) is shown for reference only: Yahoo's fields for it are internally inconsistent (reported trailing P/E 39x vs 7.6x recomputed from its market cap and net income), so it is excluded from the medians.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: AI capex digestion in 2027-28: logic and DRAM customers push out EUV orders, China DUV demand (over 30% of 2024-25 system sales) fades, and margins fall back to ~35%.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus 2026-27 as AI drives leading-edge logic and HBM/DRAM EUV layers; then mid-single-digit growth and a 42% EBIT margin (service and High-NA mix).

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: High-NA EUV (EXE:5200) is adopted at the 1.4nm node and in DRAM from 2028, with higher ASPs and service revenue.

scenarios.name: Tail: China export restrictions tighten
scenarios.desc: US/Dutch rules extend to immersion DUV servicing and spare parts for China, cutting China revenue to a fraction and stranding the installed base.

scenarios.name: Tail: High-NA everywhere + AI super-cycle
scenarios.desc: High-NA becomes standard for logic and DRAM and AI capex keeps compounding; ASML exceeds the top of its 2030 targets (€60B sales, 56-60% gross margin).

scenarios.name: Tail: Taiwan geopolitical shock
scenarios.desc: A blockade or conflict around Taiwan halts TSMC's leading-edge expansion (ASML's largest customer); ~€5B of assumed write-offs on installed tools and receivables, and a higher risk premium.

catalysts.event: Q4/FY2026 results and 2027 guidance; EUV bookings
TSMC 2027 capex guide (leading-edge and High-NA plans)
US / Dutch export-control updates for China (DUV servicing)
High-NA EUV insertion decisions (Intel 14A, TSMC A14, DRAM makers)

score.rationale: Quality: sole supplier of EUV lithography, FY2025 operating margin 34.6% and a growing installed-base service business. Growth: consensus net sales +36% in 2026 and +29% in 2027 on AI-driven logic and memory demand. Risk: lumpy orders tied to a few customers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix), China export controls and Taiwan concentration. Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside.

VST.sector: US independent power producer (nuclear, gas, retail electricity)
VST.growthNote: Year 1 / year 2 = consensus FY2026 / FY2027 revenue ($22.3B / $24.0B, +26% / +8%), boosted by acquired gas plants and data-center contracts. Reported revenue and operating income include hedge and derivative marks, so the year-1 EBIT margin is set at 20% (2026 adjusted EBITDA guide ≈ 33% of revenue less ~13% D&A incl. nuclear fuel). Steady-state EBIT margin 24% in the Base case, as nuclear PPAs with hyperscalers (Comanche Peak) lock in higher prices. Buybacks of ~$1B/yr retire ~3%/yr of shares for 3 years. The 45U nuclear production tax credit (through 2032) supports a floor on nuclear revenue and lowers the cash tax rate (18% assumed).
VST.precedentNote: Power-generation control deals (estimates): Vistra-Energy Harbor (2024, ~$3.4B), Constellation-Calpine (announced 2025, ~$26.6B EV incl. debt), NRG-LS Power gas and C&I assets (2025, ~$12B), Talen's purchases of PJM gas plants (2025). Deals have cleared around 8-13x forward EBITDA, below where listed nuclear-heavy IPPs now trade. A takeover of VST is unlikely (size, FERC/NRC approvals); this is a private-market cross-check.
VST.compsNote: Comps: CEG (nuclear-heavy, the closest peer), NRG (retail + gas), TLN (nuclear + PJM gas), plus the regulated utilities PEG and ETR as low-beta references. Utilities trade on lower multiples, which pulls down the median; reported TTM EBITDA includes hedge marks.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: Fewer and cheaper data-center PPAs than hoped, low gas prices flatten ERCOT/PJM forward curves, and PJM capacity prices fall from record levels after market-rule changes; margins revert toward pre-2024 levels.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus 2026-27, then ~6% growth as more nuclear and gas output is contracted with hyperscalers at premium prices (Comanche Peak deal as the template); the 45U nuclear PTC sets a floor; buybacks continue.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Multiple long-term nuclear PPAs (including uprates and new gas peakers co-located with data centers) re-rate the fleet as contracted infrastructure; ERCOT load growth keeps scarcity pricing high.

scenarios.name: Tail: Data-center demand bust
scenarios.desc: Hyperscalers cut AI capex or efficiency gains (smaller models, better chips) slash power needs; announced campuses are cancelled, forward power prices collapse and PPA talks stall.

scenarios.name: Tail: Nuclear outage / regulatory shock
scenarios.desc: An extended forced outage at Comanche Peak or Beaver Valley, an NRC safety order, FERC limits on behind-the-meter co-location, or repeal of the 45U PTC; ~$3B of assumed lost margin and repair costs.

scenarios.name: Tail: ERCOT price-spike event
scenarios.desc: A Winter Storm Uri-style event (Feb 2021 cost Vistra ~$1.6B): plants trip while prices hit the $5,000/MWh cap and the retail book is short; ~$2.5B one-off loss, followed by tighter market rules and higher prices.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results; 2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance and buyback update
New nuclear / gas PPAs with hyperscalers (Comanche Peak follow-ons)
PJM capacity auction results and FERC co-location rulings
ERCOT peak-demand and winter-storm risk

score.rationale: Quality: one of the largest US competitive generators (~41 GW incl. ~6.4 GW nuclear) with an integrated retail book that hedges output. Growth: consensus +26% revenue in 2026 on acquisitions and data-center demand; contracted nuclear PPAs add visibility. Risk: commodity and weather exposure (Uri), policy and FERC co-location rules, and leverage (~$20B debt). Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside.

ABEV.sector: Beverages (beer, soft drinks) - Brazil, LatAm North/South, Canada
ABEV.betaNote: Yahoo's 5Y beta (0.22) is distorted by BRL moves and local trading; an assumed 0.75 (EM consumer staples ADR) is used, plus Brazil CRP.
ABEV.growthNote: Ambev reports in BRL (IFRS 20-F). The model is computed in BRL and converted to USD per ADR (1 ADR = 1 common share; Yahoo market cap / ADR price = 15.4B shares, matching the share count) at the Banco Central do Brasil PTAX rate stored in valuation.json. Year 1 / year 2 = consensus FY2026 / FY2027 net revenue in BRL (+2.6% / +4.9%). Because the model holds the FX rate flat, mid-term growth (3.5%) is set in USD-equivalent terms, i.e. below nominal BRL growth by the expected inflation gap. Argentina (Quilmes) is reported under IAS 29 hyperinflation accounting.
ABEV.precedentNote: Brewing control deals (estimates): AB InBev-SABMiller (2016, ~$100B+), Heineken-Brasil Kirin (2017, ~€0.7B), Constellation-Grupo Modelo US business (2013, ~$4.75B), Asahi-CUB (2020, ~$11B), around 11-16x EBITDA. AB InBev already owns ~62% of Ambev, so the relevant M&A case is a minority buy-out at a premium.
ABEV.compsNote: Comps: BUD (parent), Heineken (HEINY), FEMSA (FMX, a conglomerate: OXXO retail + Coca-Cola FEMSA stake), Carlsberg (CABGY) and Constellation Brands (STZ). Multiples are recomputed in USD from Yahoo data (EUR, MXN, DKK financials converted).

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: Brazil beer volumes stay weak (consumer squeeze, weather, competition from Heineken), USD-linked costs (aluminium, barley) rise and Argentina drags on reported results; margins slip.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus 2026-27; premiumization (Corona, Spaten, Michelob Ultra), the BEES B2B platform and Zé Delivery support pricing above inflation; EBIT margin ~25%.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Volume recovery in Brazil plus cost deflation and a stronger BRL; Argentina normalizes and contributes in USD.

scenarios.name: Tail: BRL crisis
scenarios.desc: A fiscal scare sends the BRL down 25-30% and Brazil's country risk up ~300 bp; USD revenue falls and imported costs squeeze margins for two years.

scenarios.name: Tail: Tax shock
scenarios.desc: Tax reform hits harder than expected: a high Imposto Seletivo ('sin tax') on beer from 2027 and the end of interest-on-capital (JCP) deductibility, plus adverse rulings on Ambev's large tax contingencies (~$3B assumed one-off).

scenarios.name: Tail: Argentina relapse
scenarios.desc: Argentina returns to devaluation and FX controls; IAS 29 restatement and translation losses cut the LatAm South contribution and dividends from Quilmes are trapped.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results: Brazil beer volumes, margin and buyback/dividend
Start of the CBS/IBS transition and the Imposto Seletivo rates on beverages
BCB Copom rate decisions and the BRL
Argentina presidential election (Quilmes, FX regime)

score.rationale: Quality: dominant beer share in Brazil (~60%), net cash and strong cash conversion (FCF ~R$20B in 2025). Growth: low, with consensus net revenue +3% in 2026 and +5% in 2027 in BRL. Risk: BRL and Brazil country risk, tax reform, tax contingencies and Argentina. Valuation: scored from the model's implied upside.

UBER.sector: Global mobility, delivery and freight marketplace
UBER.growthNote: Revenue is driven by gross bookings (FY2025 ≈ $193B: Mobility ~47%, Delivery ~49%, Freight ~4%) times the take rate (~27% overall; Mobility ~30%, Delivery ~19% incl. advertising). Year 1 / year 2 = consensus FY2026 / FY2027 revenue ($57.9B / $66.8B), i.e. ~17-19% bookings growth with a broadly stable take rate. EBIT is GAAP operating income, so stock-based compensation (~$1.9B/yr, ~3.5% of revenue) is treated as a real cost; company 'adjusted EBITDA' (~$8.7B FY2025, ~4.5% of gross bookings) adds back SBC and is not used. Steady-state EBIT margin of 17% in the Base case (~5% of gross bookings). Buybacks under the $20B authorisation more than offset SBC: share count assumed to fall 2%/yr for 3 years. Equity stakes (Didi, Aurora, Grab residual, Lime, Moove, WeRide/Pony.ai and others) are non-operating and added in the EV bridge at balance-sheet carrying value (Yahoo 'Investments And Advances'). Cash tax rate 19% assumed (US NOLs/credits partly shelter income after the valuation-allowance release).

nonOpAssets.label: equity stakes at carrying value (Didi, Aurora, Lime, WeRide/Pony.ai, other); latest FY balance sheet, Yahoo

UBER.peNIExcludeLabel: release of the Netherlands deferred-tax-asset valuation allowance, Q3 2025 ($4.9B; verified in Uber 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-09-30, SEC accession 0001543151-25-000033)
UBER.precedentNote: Platform/marketplace control deals (estimates): Uber-Postmates (2020, $2.65B), DoorDash-Wolt (2021, ~$8B, EV/Sales-based), Uber-Trendyol Go (2025, $700M), DoorDash-Deliveroo (2025, ~$3.9B, ~15x forward EBITDA), Prosus-Just Eat Takeaway (2025, ~€4.1B). Profitable marketplaces have cleared around 15-25x EBITDA. A takeover of Uber (~$143B) is implausible; this is a private-market cross-check.
UBER.compsNote: Comps: LYFT (US mobility), DASH (delivery), GRAB (SE Asia super-app), CART (grocery delivery); ABNB and BKNG are shown as reference-only (asset-light marketplaces, not in the statistics). LYFT is excluded from P/E because its TTM net income also includes a tax valuation-allowance release; peers with EV/EBITDA above 60x (LYFT) drop out automatically.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: Bookings growth slows to mid-single digits as US Mobility matures and Delivery competition (DoorDash, Amazon, local players) forces incentives; take rate slips and insurance costs rise; margins stall near today's level.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus 2026-27 (~17-19% bookings growth), then ~10% as Mobility, Delivery and advertising grow with stable take rates; operating leverage lifts GAAP EBIT margin to ~17%; buybacks retire ~2% of shares a year.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Membership (Uber One), advertising and grocery drive faster bookings growth and a rising take rate; GAAP margins approach 21% as SBC falls as a share of revenue.

scenarios.name: Tail: Robotaxi disintermediation
scenarios.desc: Tesla and Waymo scale owned robotaxi networks city by city and sell rides directly; Uber loses the highest-density urban trips, is pushed to a low-margin aggregator role for third-party AV fleets, and Mobility bookings shrink after year 3.

scenarios.name: Tail: Driver-classification shock
scenarios.desc: A federal or major-state ruling (or EU Platform Work Directive implementation) reclassifies drivers and couriers as employees: payroll taxes, benefits and minimum pay raise unit costs, some volume is lost, and ~$5B of back-pay, tax and settlement costs is assumed.

scenarios.name: Tail: Robotaxi upside via partnerships
scenarios.desc: Partnerships (Waymo in Austin/Atlanta, WeRide, Pony.ai, Nuro/Lucid, Baidu, May Mobility and others) make Uber the demand layer for AV fleets: driver cost falls out of the trip, the platform keeps a high take rate on a cheaper, larger market, and margins move toward 24%.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results: gross bookings growth by segment, take rate, GAAP EBIT and buybacks
Tesla / Waymo robotaxi launches in new cities, and new Uber AV partnerships
Driver-classification rulings (US DOL rule, state ballots, EU Platform Work Directive transposition by Dec-2026)
Mark-to-market and monetisation of equity stakes (Didi, Aurora, WeRide, Pony.ai)

score.rationale: Quality: the largest global mobility + delivery network (~190M monthly active platform consumers), positive and growing free cash flow and an investment-grade balance sheet. Growth: high-teens bookings growth with advertising and membership. Risk: autonomous-vehicle disintermediation, labour classification, insurance costs and regulation in many cities. Valuation from the model.

BE.sector: Solid-oxide fuel cells / on-site power for data centers and industry
BE.growthNote: Bloom sells solid-oxide fuel-cell 'Energy Servers' (product + installation) and earns recurring service and electricity revenue. Year 1 / year 2 = consensus FY2026 / FY2027 revenue ($4.1B / $6.8B, +104% / +65%), driven by AI data-center on-site power (AEP up to 1 GW, Oracle, Brookfield's up to $5B Bloom deployment programme, Equinix) where grid interconnection queues are years long. Product gross margins ~35-40%, service now slightly profitable after years of losses; GAAP operating margin turned positive only in FY2024-25 (history of losses). Year-1 EBIT margin 15% (Q2-2026: 17%). Steady-state EBIT margin 20% in the Base case. SK ecoplant (Korea) remains a large distributor/customer but stopped being a related party in Jul-2025. The IRA investment tax credit (48E, fuel cells qualify through 2032 after OBBBA) lowers customers' cost per kW. Cash tax 15% (NOLs). Working capital is heavy (inventory, receivables): ΔNWC 15% of Δrevenue. SBC dilution ~2%/yr. Beta set to 2.0 (Yahoo 5y monthly beta 3.78, Blume 2.86, inflated by the 2020-21 and 2025-26 squeezes). Convertible notes are valued if-converted (see key inputs).

converts.name: 3.0% Green Convertible Senior Notes due Jun-2029
3.0% Green Convertible Senior Notes due Jun-2028

BE.convertsNote: unpaid principal and initial conversion prices from the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (SEC accession 0001628280-26-050247): 0% 2030 $2,500.0M at $194.97, 3% 2029 $27.0M at $20.84, 3% 2028 $0.8M at $18.85; capped calls on the 2028 notes ignored
BE.precedentNote: Power-equipment / clean-power control deals (estimates): Siemens Energy-Siemens Gamesa minorities (2022-23), Brookfield-Westinghouse (2023, ~$8B EV, ~3x sales), Constellation-Calpine (2025), Chart-Flowserve and Baker Hughes-Chart (2025, ~$13.6B, ~3x sales, ~13x EBITDA), Eaton-Fibrebond (2025, $1.4B, ~3.5x sales), Vertiv-Great Lakes (2024). EBITDA is too small to anchor a deal multiple, so EV/Sales of 5-10x is used (premium for data-center-power scarcity). A takeover at ~$67B is a cross-check only.
BE.compsNote: Comps: PLUG, FCEL, BLDP (fuel cells), FLNC (storage), GEV, ETN, VRT (data-center power equipment). Outlier filter: peers with negative TTM EBITDA (PLUG, FCEL, BLDP, FLNC) are shown but excluded from all statistics (their EV/Sales reflects distress, not value); EV/EBITDA above 60x and P/E above 80x are dropped as usual. The remaining set (GEV, ETN, VRT) is profitable and mature, so comps sit far below Bloom's growth-driven price.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: Data-center orders slip as grid connections and gas turbines catch up; Korea volumes fall; product margins compress on price competition and gas costs; growth slows to high single digits after 2027.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus 2026-27 (AEP, Oracle, Brookfield programmes), then ~25% growth fading as on-site power becomes a standard bridge/primary solution for AI campuses; service turns solidly profitable; EBIT margin ~20%.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Multi-GW framework deals with several hyperscalers and utilities, capacity expansion to 2 GW+/yr; scale lifts product margins above 40% and EBIT margin to ~24%.

scenarios.name: Tail: Data-center capex bust
scenarios.desc: Hyperscalers cut AI capex sharply; announced campuses are cancelled or switched back to grid/turbines; Bloom's backlog shrinks, factories run under-utilised and losses return.

scenarios.name: Tail: Loss of ITC / tax credits
scenarios.desc: Fuel-cell eligibility for the 48E ITC is repealed or curtailed (or foreign-entity rules bite), raising customers' cost per kW by ~30%; ~$0.5B of assumed recapture, indemnity and contract-repricing costs.

scenarios.name: Tail: Large hyperscaler contract win
scenarios.desc: A multi-GW, multi-year primary-power agreement directly with a hyperscaler (on the Brookfield/Oracle template) makes Bloom the default on-site power supplier for AI campuses.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results: revenue vs +100% guide, product/service margins, backlog and 2027 outlook
New hyperscaler / utility on-site power agreements (AEP, Oracle, Brookfield follow-ons)
Treasury guidance on 48E ITC and foreign-entity-of-concern rules for fuel cells
Conversion / settlement of the 0% 2030 convertible notes ($2.5B, conversion price $194.97)

score.rationale: Quality: proprietary solid-oxide technology, ~1.5 GW+ installed and a growing service annuity, but GAAP profits only since 2024 after two decades of losses. Growth: revenue roughly doubling in 2026 on AI data-center demand. Risk: concentration in data centers and Korea, dependence on tax credits, gas-price exposure for customers, a very high beta and convertible dilution. Valuation from the model.

AVGO.sector: Semiconductors (custom AI accelerators, networking) and infrastructure software (VMware)
AVGO.growthNote: Two segments: semiconductor solutions (~58% of FY2025 revenue; custom AI accelerators/XPUs for Google TPU, Meta, ByteDance, OpenAI and others, plus Tomahawk/Jericho Ethernet switching) and infrastructure software (~42%; VMware Cloud Foundation, CA, Symantec). Year 1 / year 2 = consensus FY2026 / FY2027 revenue ($106B / $174B, +66% / +64%), driven by AI semiconductor revenue (OpenAI's 10 GW custom-accelerator programme from H2-2026, Anthropic/Google TPU orders). EBIT is GAAP operating income: it is after ~$7B/yr of amortisation of acquired intangibles (mostly VMware; falls as it rolls off) and ~$7.6B of SBC (FY2025, ~12% of revenue), both treated as costs. Non-GAAP 'adjusted EBITDA' (~67% of revenue) adds both back and is not used. Year-1 GAAP EBIT margin 50% (TTM 54%; AI ASIC mix lowers gross margin), steady state 52% in the Base case. D&A falls from ~14% of revenue (amortisation-heavy) to 3% as intangibles roll off. Tax 15% (Pillar Two minimum; Singapore incentives). Share count is split-adjusted (10-for-1, Jul-2024); buybacks roughly offset SBC (0%/yr). Dividends ($2.60/share/yr) are a use of FCFF, not deducted separately. Debt (~$59B, mostly from VMware) is deducted in the EV bridge.
AVGO.precedentNote: Large semiconductor / infrastructure-software control deals (estimates): Broadcom-VMware (2023, ~$69B EV, ~17x EBITDA), AMD-Xilinx (2022, ~$49B, ~40x), Analog Devices-Maxim (2021, ~$21B, ~22x), Synopsys-Ansys (2025, ~$35B, ~35x), Broadcom-CA (2018, ~$19B, ~15x), Broadcom-Symantec enterprise (2019, $10.7B). 18-28x EBITDA is the central range. A takeover of AVGO (~$1.6T) is implausible; private-market cross-check only.
AVGO.compsNote: Comps: NVDA, AMD (merchant AI accelerators), MRVL (custom ASICs, the closest peer), QCOM, TXN, ADI (diversified analog/RF), ANET (AI networking). ORCL and MSFT are software references, shown but excluded from the statistics. Usual outlier filters: EV/EBITDA above 60x (AMD, MRVL) and P/E above 80x (AMD) drop out. Peer TTM figures are GAAP; Broadcom's TTM EBITDA is GAAP (after SBC, before amortisation).

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.desc: AI ASIC orders arrive later and smaller than consensus (OpenAI ramp slips, Google shifts TPU volume to MediaTek); VMware customers churn after the subscription price rises; growth slows to mid-single digits after FY2027 and margin settles at 45%.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.desc: Consensus FY2026-27 (AI semis roughly doubling each year, VMware high-single-digit growth), then ~15% growth fading as hyperscaler custom-silicon programmes mature; amortisation rolls off and GAAP EBIT margin holds ~52%.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.desc: Five or more XPU customers in volume and share gains in scale-out/scale-up Ethernet; AI revenue keeps compounding above 25% beyond FY2027 with software as a cash cow; margin ~56%.

scenarios.name: Tail: AI capex bust / ASIC in-sourcing
scenarios.desc: Hyperscalers cut AI capex hard and in-source chip design (Google/Meta build their own back-end teams or move to MediaTek/Alchip); AI semiconductor revenue falls back toward FY2024 levels and fixed costs compress margins.

scenarios.name: Tail: China / Taiwan (TSMC) shock
scenarios.desc: A blockade or conflict disrupts TSMC, Broadcom's sole foundry for leading-edge ASICs, or China retaliates with export bans; shipments halt for several quarters (~$30B of assumed lost profit and costs) before capacity is rebuilt elsewhere.

scenarios.name: Tail: Multi-GW ASIC ramps (OpenAI and others)
scenarios.desc: OpenAI's 10 GW programme and new multi-GW commitments (Anthropic, xAI, sovereign AI) ship on schedule; custom accelerators take a large share of AI compute from GPUs and Broadcom's AI revenue reaches several hundred billion dollars.

catalysts.event: Q4 FY2026 results: AI semiconductor revenue, FY2027 AI outlook, VMware renewals
OpenAI custom-accelerator deployment start and new XPU customer announcements
US-China export controls and Taiwan Strait tensions (TSMC supply)
Dividend increase (usually December) and buybacks; debt paydown

score.rationale: Quality: leader in custom AI accelerators and Ethernet switching, with very high margins and a large recurring software base. Growth: consensus revenue +66% in FY2026 and +64% in FY2027 on AI. Risk: customer concentration (a handful of hyperscalers), TSMC/Taiwan dependence, ~$59B of debt and VMware churn. Valuation from the model.
